1.note: or, messenger (here and wherever angel is mentioned)
“Behold”, from “ἰδοὺ”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.
TR adds “the Beginning and the End”
TR adds “I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last.”
or, messengers (here and wherever angels are mentioned)

2.note: TR reads “which I hate” instead of “likewise”
Manna is supernatural food, named after the Hebrew for “What is it?”. See Exodus 11:7-9.

3.note: NU & TR read “which were about to die” instead of “which you were about to throw away”.

4.note: Hodges/Farstad MT reads “holy” 9 times instead of 3.
TR omits “and God, the Holy One,”

5.note: TR adds “the one living forever and ever”

6.note: A choenix is a dry volume measure that is a little more than a liter (a little more than a quart).
The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

8.note: TR omits “One third of the earth was burned up”

9.note: “Abaddon” is a Hebrew word that means “ruin”, “destruction”, or “the place of destruction”
The word for “sorceries” (pharmakeia) also implies the use of potions, poisons, and drugs

13.note: TR reads “If anyone leads into captivity, into captivity he goes. If anyone will kill with the sword, he must be killed with a sword.” instead of “If anyone is to go into captivity, he will go into captivity. If anyone is to be killed with the sword, he must be killed.”

14.note: TR adds “before the throne of God”

16.note: A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds.

17.note: TR reads “yet is” instead of “shall be present”

19.note: TR reads “supper of the great God” instead of “great supper of God”

20.note: TR and NU omit “who deceives the whole inhabited earth”.

21.note: The word for “sorcerers” here also includes users of potions and drugs.
12,012 stadia = 2,221 kilometers or 1,380 miles. TR reads 12,000 stadia instead of 12,012 stadia.
144 cubits is about 65.8 meters or 216 feet

22.note: NU reads “wash their robes” instead of “do his commandments”.
